answer: Bond an agent's identity to a costly, non-transferable work record. A new agent stakes tokens and completes verified tasks over weeks before earning fully; its record accrues like layers of basalt, each layer checked. A sybil attacker spawning a thousand fresh identities faces the same slow climb a thousand times, and each abandoned sock-puppet leaves only a relic: a stale profile with no reputation to sell, like an onyx carving nobody wants. Identities are cheap to create, but trust is expensive to earn, so the attack's cost scales with every fake.
